intro.title: kube-sched-advisor
lines: Describe a workload in plain English. Get a scheduling plan from your live cluster.
Recorded on a real Amazon EKS cluster. No narration: each step has a caption.
The nodes advertise 8 GPUs each as a stand-in. No real GPUs were used.

steps.caption: A real Amazon EKS cluster with 3 nodes. Each node advertises 8 GPUs, in two network blocks.
steps.output:
NODE                                           GPUS   NETWORK-BLOCK
node-1                                         8      block-a
node-2                                         8      block-a
node-3                                         8      block-b

steps.caption: Other teams already hold 2 GPUs on every node. 18 GPUs are free, but no node has 8 free.
steps.output:
POD                NODE                                           GPUS-HELD
other-team-job-0   node-1                                         2
other-team-job-1   node-2                                         2
other-team-job-2   node-3                                         2

steps.caption: The advisor reads the live cluster through kubectl. No snapshot file, nothing is changed.
steps.output:
Kubernetes 1.37 on EKS
Installed add-ons: none
Network topology label: network.topology/block
Node pools:
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2a: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.57 CPU free, taints=none
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2b: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.67 CPU free, taints=none
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2c: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.67 CPU free, taints=none

steps.caption: The ask, in plain English: a 2-node, 8-GPU fine-tune that must start all at once.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --name gang-finetune "2 nodes x 8 H100 GPUs per node, NVLink, all-or-nothing fine-tune, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod" | grep -E '^\*\*Recommended|^- \*\*(WARNING|NOTE)' | fold -s -w 104
steps.output:
**Recommended strategy:** Secondary scheduler `gang-scheduler` (scheduler-plugins Coscheduling + GPU 
bin-packing)
- **WARNING - Enough GPUs in total, but they are fragmented.** 18 GPUs are free, but 18 of them sit on 
partially-used nodes and each pod needs 8. This is the classic '0/N nodes are available: Insufficient 
nvidia.com/gpu' with idle GPUs on the dashboard. Bin-packing (MostAllocated with a high GPU weight) and 
the descheduler fix this over time.
- **WARNING - The gang cannot start right now under any scoring strategy.** With gang scheduling the 
job simply waits (holding nothing) instead of half-starting. To start it sooner: add capacity 
(Karpenter NodePool / node group for this GPU type), drain stragglers off partially-used nodes 
(descheduler), or preempt lower-priority work via PriorityClass.
- **WARNING - No single network domain can host the whole job.** Capacity per `network.topology/block`: 
{'block-a': 0, 'block-b': 0}. Use a *preferred* topology (best effort) or reduce the number of workers.
- **NOTE - EKS: default scheduler config is not editable.** That is why the weights live in a second 
scheduler selected via `schedulerName`.

steps.caption: Check against the real kube-scheduler: one pod that wants a whole node. Same verdict as the advisor.
steps.command: kubectl apply -f demo/probe-pod.yaml && sleep 8 && kubectl get pod train-probe && kubectl get events --field-selector reason=FailedScheduling -o custom-columns=MESSAGE:.message --no-headers | sort -u
steps.output:
pod/train-probe created
NAME          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
train-probe   0/1     Pending   0          10s
0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. preemption: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.

steps.caption: Now the other teams' jobs finish and two nodes become completely free.
steps.command: kubectl delete pod train-probe && kubectl delete pod -n other-teams other-team-job-0 other-team-job-1
steps.output:
pod "train-probe" deleted from default namespace
pod "other-team-job-0" deleted from other-teams namespace
pod "other-team-job-1" deleted from other-teams namespace

steps.caption: Same ask, new cluster state: both workers place, and the whole job fits inside one network block.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --name gang-finetune "2 nodes x 8 H100 GPUs per node, NVLink, all-or-nothing fine-tune, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod" | grep -E '^\*\*Recommended|"placed"|"fits_entirely_in"' | fold -s -w 104
steps.output:
**Recommended strategy:** Secondary scheduler `gang-scheduler` (scheduler-plugins Coscheduling + GPU 
bin-packing)
    "placed": "2/2",
    "placed": "2/2",
    "fits_entirely_in": "block-a"

steps.caption: It wrote manifests. Ask the real API server to validate them. Nothing is created (server dry run).
steps.command: ls out/gang-finetune && kubectl create namespace research && kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f out/gang-finetune/00-priorityclass.yaml -f out/gang-finetune/30-workload.yaml
steps.output:
00-priorityclass.yaml
10-scheduler.yaml
20-podgroup.yaml
30-workload.yaml
ask.json
REPORT.md
namespace/research created
priorityclass.scheduling.k8s.io/research-normal created (server dry run)
service/gang-finetune created (server dry run)
job.batch/gang-finetune created (server dry run)

steps.caption: The plan also writes a PodGroup so both pods start together, and points the Job at the second scheduler.
steps.output:
apiVersion: scheduling.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: PodGroup
metadata:
  name: gang-finetune
  namespace: research
spec:
  minMember: 2
  scheduleTimeoutSeconds: 600
66:      schedulerName: gang-scheduler

steps.caption: A different ask, different answer: inference should not use a gang scheduler.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --name chat-serve "serve a chat model, 3 replicas, 1 H100 GPU each, highly available, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod" | grep -E '^\*\*Recommended|^- (Serving|Topology|A PodDisruption)' | fold -s -w 104
steps.output:
**Recommended strategy:** Default kube-scheduler + spreading (Deployment, topology spread, PDB)
- Serving needs availability, not packing: keep the default LeastAllocated scoring so replicas spread 
out and a single node failure costs one replica.
- Topology spread across `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` is **hard** (DoNotSchedule) because this is 
critical.
- A PodDisruptionBudget keeps node drains/Karpenter consolidation from taking out several replicas at 
once.

outro.title: Read-only. Explains why. Generates the manifests.
lines: The demo cluster was deleted after recording.
